metadata.title: Minutes of the Meeting: What an AI Is Handed
metadata.clock: MEASURED: Kokoro audio (mp3/timings.json) and Whisper word times (_motion/plan.json); not hand-edited
metadata.note: words come from SCRIPT.md (Gate P signed, draft 2); figures on slates are read from the merged repository, never typed

beats.title: COLD OPEN, the last line
beats.narration_text: This is the last line of a message an AI is about to receive. "Your action plan must strictly match: sell." A workflow writes that line, to hold a model to a verdict it has already been given. So who decided the verdict? Let me take you to the meeting.
beats.on_screen: the closing lines of the briefing, typeset as plain text; the line `IMPORTANT: Your action_plan.immediate must strictly match "SELL". If HOLD — say hold, do not say enter.` is highlighted. Evidence panel: `simulation-results.json`, c11, last line of `ai_prompt`. Label: "From the sample run · invented company".

reveal_cues.phrase: your action plan must strictly match

beats.title: WHAT THIS IS
beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Tanmay Kulkarni, in for Humanitarians AI. This week I contributed to Mycroft, a book and a working repository of finance pipelines. It calls them recipes. One of them, the What-If Simulation Agent, asks three different questions about a stock, then hands an AI the answers. Three voices, one written record, and one question for this whole video: who had a vote, and how much? My pull request, now merged, made the six steps before the AI runnable on test data, with checks. Every company you'll see is invented, and none of this is investment advice.
beats.on_screen: "Mycroft: both a book and a working agentic repository" (README line quoted); the recipe name; a strip of six steps, then a seventh box "AI", greyed; "PR #70 · merged"; "Every company and number in this video is invented. Not investment advice."

reveal_cues.phrase: a book and a working repository
then hands an AI the answers
who had a vote, and how much
every company you'll see is invented

beats.title: THE CHAIR OPENS
beats.narration_text: Today's stock is Ironbridge Power. Invented. Growth, five percent. Sentiment, point three five. A price-to-earnings of eighty, and an aggressive investor. I'll call the workflow the chair, and the three simulators its voices. The chair's first job is to make sure every seat has something to read. Ironbridge arrived with everything filled in. But if a request arrives with nothing, the chair fills every seat itself. A company called Unknown Company, growth fifteen percent, sentiment point five. The meeting starts anyway.
beats.on_screen: the request as a small card (Ironbridge Power, IRB, growth 5%, sentiment 0.35, P/E 80, D/E 1.5, risk "high"); a second, empty card that fills in with the defaults (Unknown Company, N/A, 15%, 0.5, 25, 0.5, "medium"). Caption: "defaults, as the workflow's first step defines them". Evidence panel: `c06-empty-body-all-defaults` result; `validate-audit.md` ("fields filled by the workflow's defaults"). Label: "Invented · not a real company".

reveal_cues.phrase: i'll call the workflow the chair
if a request arrives with nothing

beats.title: FIRST VOICE
beats.narration_text: First voice: growth against sentiment. It sorts a stock into one of nine boxes, low, medium or high on each. Ironbridge is low and low. The voice says strong sell, with eighty-two percent confidence.
beats.on_screen: the 3×3 grid, the LOW/LOW cell highlighted; "Sim 1 · STRONG_SELL · 82%". Evidence panel: `simulation-results.json`, c11 `sim1_growth_sentiment`. Label: "Invented".

beats.title: SECOND VOICE
beats.narration_text: Second voice: the same stock, judged for three kinds of investor. Conservative says avoid. Balanced says avoid. Aggressive has the loosest limits. Growth at least five percent. Sentiment at least point three five. Price-to-earnings no more than eighty. Debt to equity no more than one and a half. And Ironbridge sits exactly on all four. Four out of four. Enter a full position.
beats.on_screen: three seats (Conservative: AVOID; Balanced: AVOID; Aggressive: ENTER); the aggressive seat's four criteria ticking one at a time, each showing actual against limit (5% ≥ 5%, 0.35 ≥ 0.35, 80 ≤ 80, 1.50 ≤ 1.5). Evidence panel: c11 `criteria_evaluation`. Label: "Invented".

reveal_cues.phrase: sentiment at least point three five
debt to equity no more than one and a half

beats.title: THIRD VOICE
beats.narration_text: Third voice, and this one asks something different. Not what should we do, but how close is it to changing its mind. It nudges growth and sentiment up and down, six ways, and watches the verdict. Three of the six nudges change it. The stability score: point oh five, out of one.
beats.on_screen: six small nudges, three flipping their label; a stability gauge near zero, "0.05 / 1.0". Evidence panel: c11 `sim3_threshold_break` (`stress_breach_count`, `stability_score`). Label: "Invented".

reveal_cues.phrase: how close is it to changing its mind
three of the six nudges change it

beats.title: THEY DISAGREE
beats.narration_text: Now they disagree. The first voice says strong sell. The second says enter a full position. Nobody has made a mistake. They were asked different questions. So the chair weighs them: forty-five, thirty-five and twenty. The chair's scale runs from one to five. Strong sell sits at the bottom, and enter a full position at the top. So a smaller weight on the top can outweigh a bigger weight on the bottom. The voices contribute point three seven, one point seven five, and point oh five. Together, two point one seven out of five. Anywhere from one point eight to two point eight, the chair writes down as sell.
beats.on_screen: the three voices' verdicts side by side; the three weights; the three weighted pieces summing to 2.17; a ruler showing 1.8 to 2.8 labelled SELL; the chair's pen writing "SELL"; the five-point scale drawn once, STRONG_SELL at the bottom and ENTER_FULL_POSITION at the top. Evidence panel: c11 `aggregate` (`component_scores`, `score`, `final_recommendation`). Label: "Invented".

reveal_cues.phrase: the first voice says strong sell
the chair's scale runs from one to five

beats.title: THE MINUTES
beats.narration_text: Then the chair writes the minutes. About four hundred and seventy words. The stock, each voice, the stress tests, the verdict. And one last instruction, for someone who wasn't in the room: the action plan must strictly match sell. The AI only ever receives the minutes. And in the minutes, a number somebody typed looks exactly like a number the chair filled in.
beats.on_screen: the briefing scrolling past in miniature, its sections labelled (company profile, the three simulations, aggregate verdict); the final line highlighted again; two numbers side by side, "0.5 (typed)" and "0.5 (filled in by default)", rendered identically in the briefing. Evidence panel: c06 `ai_prompt` ("Sentiment Score: 0.5/1.0"). Label: "Invented".

reveal_cues.phrase: then the chair writes the minutes
about four hundred and seventy words
looks exactly like a number the chair

beats.title: THE TURN, MY MINUTE-TAKER
beats.narration_text: Here's where I got something wrong. To check the original, I wrote a second minute-taker, a Python copy of those six steps, and ran both on the same meetings. On two requests, it wrote a different verdict. Those were requests where growth was typed as the letters A, B, C, and sentiment was left as empty text. Python and JavaScript disagree about the smallest of a list when one entry isn't a number. I fixed it. Now both write the same minutes, to the letter, on all twenty-three requests, and a test keeps that slip from coming back.
beats.on_screen: two columns of minutes, "original" and "mine", one verdict line differing, then equal; "21 of 23 → 23 of 23"; the self-test row "BREAK: min/max with NaN … caught". Evidence panel: `logs/RUN_LOG.md` 2026-10-17 "Fixed while building"; `parity-results.json` (23/23).

beats.title: ADJOURNED
beats.narration_text: Nothing was sent anywhere. The step that would call the AI, and the step that would save the answer, are written down as hand-offs, marked not approved. Five items in the recipe are still open, and it still says draft, on purpose.
beats.on_screen: the two hand-offs with `approved_for_live_action: false`; the recipe's frontmatter (`status: DRAFT`, `todos_open: 5`). Evidence panel: `run-approved-tools-2026-10-17.json` (`live_handoffs`); the recipe's frontmatter.

reveal_cues.phrase: the step that would call the ai
five items in the recipe are still open

beats.title: CLOSE
beats.narration_text: If an AI is going to summarise your next meeting, have you read the minutes? Who had a vote? And how much of one? A good answer names the voices and their weights. "The AI will figure it out" doesn't count.
beats.on_screen: the minutes, dimmed; the three questions.

beats.title: OUTRO
beats.narration_text: Adjourned. Tanmay Kulkarni, in for Humanitarians AI, signing off.
